passage: On Sunday after lunch Rajni put the camp brochure beside the shop ledger on the table. “Papa, before you say anything, let me show you why this matters, and then you tell me what June really looks like at the shop.” Yusuf raised his eyebrows. Rajni explained that the camp certificate counted for the science-college forms. Yusuf turned the ledger pages slowly. “The heavy weeks are only the last ten days of the month, when new stock comes in,” he said. Rajni blinked; the picture in Rajni's head had been the whole month. “And I did not know the certificate was for admissions,” Yusuf said. Neither had expected that. They wrote both sets of dates on one sheet and agreed to check the camp calendar together on Monday.

qa.q: When are the heavy weeks at the shop?
qa.a: The last ten days of the month, when new stock comes in.

qa.q: What did Rajni feel when Yusuf described the busy weeks?
qa.a: Surprise: Rajni blinked, because the busy time was much shorter than the whole month Rajni had imagined.

qa.q: Why did asking and listening work better than guessing?
qa.a: A written comparison of the real dates let both sides check the actual needs before deciding, instead of each assuming the worst.

qa.q: How does the talk look to Yusuf?
qa.a: Yusuf learns something new, that the certificate matters for admissions, and sees Rajni asking about the shop, so he has a reason to take the camp seriously.

grounding: A student explains what the camp means, asks what the shop needs and listens, so nobody is surprised.

passage:
"Amma, Papa, can we talk before you decide about the camp?" Swati asked after dinner, pulling a chair to the table.

Her mother, Leela, sighed. "The shop needs you in May. You know that."

"I know. But can I explain first?" Swati put a printout down. "This coding camp gives a certificate the college looks at. It's three weeks. If I get into computer science, that's why."

Her father looked at the paper. "We didn't know it was connected to college."

"So what does the shop really need?" Swati asked. "Every day? Or the weekends? Or just the stock-taking?"

Leela paused. "Mostly the Saturday rush and the stock-taking at the end of May."

"The camp ends on the 24th."

Her parents looked at each other. "Then we have something to talk about," her father said.

qa.q: How did Leela seem to feel when Swati first raised the camp?
qa.a: Leela seemed tired and a bit resistant, sighing because she expected a fight about the shop.

qa.q: What else could Swati offer to show she takes the shop's needs seriously?
qa.a: She could offer to cover the Saturday rushes after the camp and all of the stock-taking, so her parents see a concrete plan.

qa.q: How might Swati's father see the camp after the conversation?
qa.a: Her father now sees it as linked to college, not just a holiday, which makes him willing to talk it through.

grounding: Shows a student explaining what a camp means for future study, asking about the shop's actual needs and listening, so both sides see the other's stakes.

passage:
Last year my parents wanted me at our electronics repair shop for the whole summer, and I wanted the physics olympiad camp in Mumbai. I'm Suraj, and my first instinct was to sulk. My sister Devika talked me out of it.

"Just talk to them properly," she said. "Explain. And ask what they actually need."

So one Sunday morning, before the shop opened, I sat with Appa and Amma. I told them the camp was ten days, and that it could help me get into a good science college. Then I asked, "What does the shop need from me, really?"

Appa thought. "The festival season orders. Mid-June."

The camp was in late May. Neither of us had known the other's dates. Amma laughed.

It wasn't magic. But because I explained and listened, nobody was surprised, and nobody felt ignored.

qa.q: How long was the olympiad camp?
How did Suraj feel at first about the request to stay at the shop?
qa.a: Suraj felt sulky and resentful, wanting the camp and expecting a clash.

qa.q: What else could Suraj have asked during the talk?
qa.a: Suraj could have asked how the shop managed last year, to see what help is really needed and when.

qa.q: How might Amma have felt when they realised the dates didn't clash?
qa.a: Amma seems relieved and amused, laughing when the two needs turned out to fit.

grounding: A reflective account of a student explaining what a camp means for future study and asking about the shop's real needs, so both sides understand each other's stakes.
